content:
mae (PM): Quick sync 1 we heard during testing that the roles grid is cramped on smaller laptops. We need low-effort options to improve readability and a clear plan for SSO copy in the invite flow.
josh (FE): On 1366x768 it collapses badly. Two ideas: reduce column count at <1280px OR switch to a stacked card list with key info. Cards might be nicer for touch screens.
ananya (Design): I sketched both. Cards emphasize role name, members, and primary actions; details (last activity, owner, notes) go into an overflow menu. Cards increase vertical space but feel less dense. Link: https://figma.redwood/roles/cards-vs-grid
rory (A11Y): Cards are fine keyboard-wise if we make the card itself focusable and expose an actions menu. Must ensure focus-visible is obvious and role badges meet contrast >= 4.5:1. Current green badge fails with gray text.
lina (Eng): Implementation concerns: cards change DOM order and may affect virtualization. If we keep grid, collapsing columns is cheaper. For either approach, we should lazy-render per-row menus and paginate/virtualize 10k+ rows.
mae (PM): Let's pick the lowest-risk pattern to ship quickly and iterate. Josh/Lina, can you prototype column collapse first?
josh (FE): Yep. Plan: collapse 'Last activity' and 'Notes' into a "More" menu at <1200px. Show: role name, members, status, actions.
ananya (Design): Also proposing copy tweak for SSO: change label from "SSO enforcement" to "Require SSO to sign in" and CTA in sidebar from "Manage SSO" to "SSO & authentication" as users expect. In-invite microcopy: when org requires SSO, show banner: "This organization requires SSO. Invited users must sign in with your SSO provider." with link to docs.
rory (A11Y): For the banner, use role=alert and ensure it is announced by screen readers. For the toggle, attach an accessible description instead of relying solely on tooltip: aria-describedby -> hidden span explaining enforcement implications. Example snippet I can paste into the design doc.
pete (QA): Found a bug in audit logs: when filtering by event type and then using browser back, the UI resets filters and focus. We need to persist filters in the URL and restore focus to the active filter chip on popstate.
lina (Eng): Agreed. We'll persist filters as query params and programmatically focus the first active chip after history restore.
mae (PM): Two policy questions: 1) Should SSO enforcement be org-level default with invite-level override? 2) How explicit should override warnings be?
ananya (Design): Recommend org-level enforcement. Allow per-invite override only for exceptions and show an inline warning: "Warning: this invite bypasses org SSO and will allow email/password sign-in. Learn more." Keep the warning prominent (icon + yellow background).
josh (FE): Small UX detail: avoid opening multiple modals for override explanations. Use an inline expandable panel in the invite modal.
rory (A11Y): Make sure the expandable panel is accessible: aria-expanded on the trigger and focus moves into panel content when opened. Also add aria-live polite for status updates.
pete (QA): I'll add these to regression cases: keyboard tab order, aria-invalid on form errors, aria-describedby for tooltips, banner role=alert announcement, and URL filter restore.
lina (Eng): Schedule: spike for collapse + url state + a11y checklist by EOD Friday. I'll include perf numbers for large orgs.
josh (FE): I'll prototype and pair with Lina.
ananya (Design): I'll deliver updated mocks, copy, and a11y markup notes tonight.
rory (A11Y): I'll run a quick keyboard + NVDA walkthrough and share notes tomorrow morning.
mae (PM): Excellent. Thanks team. One tiny copy nit to include: change "Invite users" CTA in header to "Invite team" per research.
ananya (Design): Noted, updating mocks.
pete (QA): Will schedule regression tests after spike validation next week.
mae (PM): Great work :thumbsup:
